messageLessFailures._why: A continuation can fail before producing a transcript row. Saved diagnostics must remain visible after the live error card is cleared or the conversation is reopened.

idleRetirement._why: Unviewed idle runtime handles expire independently of later requests. Mounted views have owner-scoped tokens, and all ongoing work and live mobile followers retain their handle. Reopening uses the existing cold recovery path.

closeRecovery._why: A timed-out close continues draining server-side. Retain and fence its writer until a repeated close confirms teardown; scoped reads hold their lifecycle lease through the RPC.

startupRecovery._why: Activation failure has one rollback owner. Unknown live handles count as closed; uncertain cleanup retains ownership and blocks inference instead of losing the writer. Failed idle candidates back off without blocking unrelated chats.

preparation._why: Readiness waits for restored core publication without fetching task or history data. Deadlines detach only the waiter; retries keep the same endpoint and writer, and inference stays fenced until activation finishes.

terminalPersistence._why: A terminal notification must not precede the writer acknowledgement for its original messages and lifecycle record. Provider-free history reads remain read-only. Storage failures publish failure and preserve the original diagnostic and timing metadata.

resumeLedger._why: Consuming the previous run must not close the ledger used by this run. New work coexists with unresolved recovery; only confirmed continuations or settled tails leave the file, while failed recovery remains retryable.
